episodes.180155: Isolated pockets of thunderstorms developed along a stationary front across southeastern North Dakota during the late afternoon on June 7th, and then congealed as they drifted south into northeastern South Dakota. Two weather stations recorded severe-level wind gusts in Marshall and Roberts Counties, prior to the complex's dissipation during the early evening.

episodes.180386: During the afternoon and evening hours of the 7th, clusters of severe storms moved from the NW to the S through Eastern North Dakota. These storms produced large hail and wind damage across Eastern North Dakota.
episodes.180414: Mainly between 2-7 p.m. CDT on this Thursday afternoon and early evening, isolated to scattered thunderstorms drifted slowly southward across South Central Nebraska, affecting various locations mainly along and west of a line from Ord-Grand Island-Hebron. Most storms were non-severe, producing only welcomed rain, breezy winds and perhaps very small hail. However, a few storms briefly became strong to severe. Most notably, a localized downburst produced measured 76 MPH winds near Davenport in Thayer County (unofficial mesonet), with these intense speeds substantiated by a ground-truth report of some flipped irrigation pivots in the area. Other storm reports included an unofficial mesonet gust of 58 MPH near Harvard and penny size hail on the west side of Grand Island. ||This event was a classic case of diurnally-driven, pulse thunderstorm activity, firing up during peak afternoon heating and fading away as sunset approached. In the mid-upper levels, wind fields were unusually-weak by early June standards, thanks to South Central Nebraska residing under broad ridging centered north-to-south over the heart of the Central Plains. As a result, this convection was almost sparked by a combination of diurnal instability and modest convergence along a weak surface front stretched across the heart of the local area from north-northwest to south-southeast. By early-mid afternoon, the combination of temperatures climbing into the low-90s (F) and dewpoints pooling into at least the low-60s near the boundary promoted mixed-layer CAPE of 1000-2000 J/kg. Although this was sufficient instability to initiate relatively spotty convection, including a few strong to very isolated severe storms, convective intensity was significantly held in check by unseasonably weak deep-layer wind shear of at most 20 knots.
episodes.180668: A stationary front parked across the state of Arkansas coupled in tandem with an upper level pattern that kept the Natural State just ahead of an approaching trough. The result were the severe weather modes of flash flooding, severe hail, and severe winds.
episodes.180815: Anomalous atmospheric moisture combined with slow moving thunderstorms caused copious amounts of rain and in some places flooding.
episodes.180952: A thunderstorm 8 to 10 miles north/northwest of Reed Point produced heavy rainfall resulting in flash flooding that affected West White Beaver Creek. The flash flood created some log jams and took out some fencing.
episodes.180953: A very moist, easterly surface flow continued into the start of the second week of June. This resulted in dewpoints well above 50 degrees, as well as atmospheric precipitable waters over 1.00. Winds aloft continued to be light resulting in slow-moving, heavy thunderstorms. As a result, multiple flash flood events occurred across portions of central and south central Montana.
episodes.180977: A slow-moving upper level disturbance generated afternoon and evening thunderstorms across much of the region on June 7th & 8th. Multiple outflow boundary mergers kept the storms going until around 10 PM or so. Most of these storms were sub-severe, but a few were able to generate damaging downbursts and hail around 1.
episodes.181006: An isolated thunderstorm passing through Bottineau County produced wind gusts of 64 mph at the NDAWN weather station to the south-southeast of Roth.
episodes.181007: Thunderstorms formed during the afternoon and evening hours as a surface low passed through southwest and south central North Dakota. Some of these storms became severe with the primary impacts being from large hail, though severe wind gusts of 60 mph were reported on the initial severe storm in McLean County. The largest hail reported was the size of a ping pong ball, which fell in McIntosh County.
episodes.181180: Scattered thunderstorms occurred across the coastal waters, a few of which produced gusty winds in excess of 34 knots as well as a couple of waterspouts.
episodes.181472: The remnants of the previous night���s mesoscale convective vortex moved into a conditionally unstable airmass and generated thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.181511: Several rounds of rain and thunderstorms affected much of Montana during the first half of June. Flash flooding occurred across portions of the region, especially across Fergus County as well as the Rocky Mountains. Fergus County was hit exceptionally hard as several days of occasional heavy rain exasperated area creeks and streams. Casino Creek, located south of Lewistown, was washed out in at least two locations with significant road repairs required. Cottonwood Creek to the west of Casino Creek completely washed out Cotton Creek Road in several areas. Across the Rocky Mountains, easterly flow compressed moisture along the Rocky Mountain Front Range resulting in heavy rainfall and thunderstorms. Several debris flows were reported. Portions of Glacier National Park were temporarily closed due to rock slides and debris flows. The Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest also reported several flooding impacts. Across Meagher and Broadwater Counties, heavy rain affected the Woods Creek and Deep Creek burn scar areas, resulting in flash flooding along Highway 12. Flash flooding also occurred just south of Great Falls along Wilson Butte Road from a rapidly developing thunderstorm that produced 1.37 inches of rain in less than an hour at a NWS employee's home along Wilson Butte Road. A brief tornado also occurred across rural Hill County and was greatly photographed, but no damage was reported.
episodes.181520: A complex of showers and thunderstorms moved southeast through portions of the Texas Panhandle during the overnight period of June 7th-8th. This complex moved fairly quickly only dropping 0.5 up to around 0.75 of rain. However, Amarillo had already seen its storage and playa lakes at capacity. This system sent many areas near lakes into some historical flooding with residents being evacuated from some of these areas early in the morning on the 8th.
episodes.181545: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a trough of low pressure produced large hail and damaging winds across portions of central, south central and eastern Virginia.
episodes.181554: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a trough of low pressure produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.181678: Low pressure over Southern California brought significant amounts of atmospheric moisture northward over the mountains, producing showers and thunderstorms with locally heavy rain and small hail. A period of heavy rain from thunderstorms over western Plumas County produced a debris flow over Feather River Canyon. Heavy rain also led to minor street and poor drainage flooding in the Quincy area.
episodes.181801: A stationary frontal system positioned over the southeastern United States led to plentiful moisture and instability which resulted in conditions for numerous showers and thunderstorms throughout the day across southern Florida.
episodes.181839: Pop-up showers and thunderstorms over southern Delaware produced large hail.
episodes.182004: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced high winds.
episodes.182151: A weak disturbance within the sub-tropical jet stream and a stationary front across the Permian Basin aided in the development of numerous afternoon and evening thunderstorms. These thunderstorms produced large hail, severe winds, and flash flooding across portions of the region.
episodes.182214: A low pressure trough and sea breeze circulation within an environment displaying favorable instability and shear led to severe thunderstorms across southeast South Carolina.
episodes.182215: A low pressure trough within an environment displaying favorable instability and shear led to severe thunderstorms across coastal waters.
episodes.182216: A weak cold front and sea breeze circulation placed within an environment displaying modest instability and shear led to severe thunderstorms across southeast Georgia.
episodes.182390: Diurnal development of isolated storms occurred once again, in an environment of very weak shear and modest MLCAPE.  With an environment which featured considerable dry air at lower levels, a brief outflow pulse developed which resulted in wind damage.
episodes.182391: A weak impulse dropped southward along the western side of a Great Lakes closed mid-level low, igniting isolated storms overnight.  Weak shear and evaporation within a low-level dry airmass resulted in localized damaging wind gusts with the strongest storm.
episodes.182395: A backdoor cold front moving in from the northeast, provided the lift needed to support scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Upper level soundings that day showed cool enough temperatures to be supportive for hail.
episodes.182402: A weak impulse dropped southward along the western side of a Great Lakes closed mid-level low, igniting isolated storms overnight. Weak shear and evaporation within a low-level dry airmass resulted in localized damaging wind gusts with the strongest storm.
episodes.182728: Widespread thunderstorm activity across North Idaho. It brought several reports of damage, power outages, and large hail. It briefly generated a funnel cloud in the North of Hayden Idaho.
episodes.182729: Widespread thunderstorm activity across Eastern Washington. It brought several reports of damage and power outages.
episodes.182742: Severe thunderstorm winds and funnel clouds occurred on the 8th.
episodes.182811: The beginning of a very wet month began with flash flooding and a few severe weather reports in early June. There was a closed low pressure located over California bringing Pacific based moisture over southern Colorado.
episodes.182864: Scattered showers and thunderstorms enhanced by the presence of an upper level trough over the central Gulf of Mexico produced isolated waterspouts and gale-force wind gusts in the Florida Keys coastal waters.
episodes.182885: A stationary frontal system positioned over the southeastern United States led to plentiful moisture and instability which resulted in conditions for numerous showers and thunderstorms throughout the day across southern Florida and the adjacent waters.
episodes.185312: A compact upper low shifting eastward out of region leaving a moist and unstable airmass. The anomalous higher PWATS (90-95th percentile) and CAPE favored scattered thunderstorms across the region with heavy rainfall cores capable of flash flooding, gusty and erratic outflow winds, small hail, and lightning.
